turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Hey, Marcus here. You've got about twenty minutes.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Thanks, Marcus. I understand new AEs take seven months to ramp—how much of that delay is tied to reps leaving before becoming productive?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I don’t have that number. Seven months is our average time to first closed deal, not necessarily full productivity.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Got it, thanks for clarifying. What tends to consume those seven months—product knowledge, sales skills, or getting enough live opportunities?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Mostly product knowledge. They get opportunities, but they tend to fumble integration questions once customer technical teams join the call.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: How are they practicing those integration conversations today, and what typically happens when they fumble one?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Mostly they read docs, shadow calls, and do ad hoc roleplays with their manager. When they miss one, an SE has to follow up later, and we lose momentum.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Roughly how often does that happen, and is the bigger concern SE time or deals slowing down?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I don’t have a clean percentage, but it’s common enough to be a pattern. The bigger concern is deals slowing down; SE time is secondary.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: That’s where HyperSale helps: AEs rehearse technical-buyer conversations, with every score tied to exact quotes. Would fewer integration misses shorten time to first deal?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Potentially. How does that actually work?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: We turn your integration material into realistic voice scenarios; reps practice and get scored feedback citing exact quotes. Who would validate technical accuracy?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Our SE lead would validate the scenarios, with engineering weighing in on edge cases. How is this different from roleplaying with a manager?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Manager roleplays are valuable; HyperSale makes them on-demand, consistent, and evidence-based, without manager scheduling. Are they happening often enough today?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: No. They’re sporadic—usually before a high-stakes call or after something has already gone wrong.
